extractor.prompt: Stage 1 extraction, theme fundierung (founding of higher-order objectivities), one commentary.
extractor.note: Re-extracted with claude-opus-5. Replaces the 2026-09-11 pass, whose coverage note cited paragraph ranges that fell outside the one section its units came from, and whose closing unit quoted step (i) of a three-step dialectic as if it were the commentary's own thesis.

coverage_note: Scanned § II (lines 57-140) and § VII (lines 289-368), the two densest sections for this theme. §§ I, III-VI and VIII-XI are not covered.

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § II
units.term: Abbau of the sedimentations of mathematized nature
units.claim: The radicalist exigency demands that the sedimentations on which the infinite mathematization of nature was founded be themselves undone.
units.quote: the *sedimentations on which the enterprise of an infinite mathematization of nature was founded* be themselves *undone* (*défaites*)

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § II
units.claim: The question in return moves back to the originally sense-bestowing production which operates as idealization on the archi-ground of all theoretical and practical life.
units.quote: *originally sense-bestowing production* which operates, as *idealization*, on the *archi-ground* (*archi-sol*, *Urboden*) of all theoretical and practical life — the ground of the immediately intuitive world (here, specifically, of the empirically intuitive world of bodies) — and furnishes the ideal formations of geometry.

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § II
units.claim: A geological metaphor of sedimentation, deposits, levels, strata and substructures of sense runs through the text.
units.quote: *geological metaphor* that runs through the text, with its multiplied allusions to *sedimentation*, deposits, levels (*étages*), strata (*couches*), and substructures (*soubassements*) of sense.

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § II
units.term: géométrie en train de se fonder
units.claim: Kant's account instructs us about the sense of ready-made geometry but not about geometry in the process of founding itself.
units.quote: it instructs us about the sense of *ready-made geometry as such*, but not about *geometry in the process of founding itself* (*la géométrie en train de se fonder*).

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § II
units.claim: The Kantian construction yields the history of an operation and not of a founding, deploying explicitation within a space of possibility already opened.
units.quote: But it is the history of an *operation*, not of a *founding* (*l'histoire d'une opération et non d'une fondation*): it deploys gestures of explicitation within the space of a possibility *already opened* to the geometer.

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § II
units.term: founding sense withheld from psychological experience
units.claim: At the stage of the Logical Investigations no psychological experience and no event-content had, as such, a founding sense.
units.quote: no psychological experience, no event-content had, *as such*, a founding sense

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § II
units.claim: The early relation of ideality to perception is described only negatively, as non-dependence; the positive foundation of truth is not itself sought.
units.quote: it is the *non-dependence* that is underlined; the *positive foundation* of the truth is not sought for itself — one simply reduces, within the mathematical "phenomenon," what cannot presently be retained as foundation.

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § II
units.term: Urstiftung as the foundation Descartes delegated to God
units.claim: Where Descartes delegates the foundation of evidence to a veracious God, Husserl seeks that foundation in historical acts of originary founding.
units.quote: Husserl, after an analogous descriptive stage, will seek that foundation *in historical acts of originary founding* (*Urstiftung*).

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § II
units.term: proto-idealizations on the substrate of a perceived world
units.claim: If idealities neither pre-exist every subjective act nor lack a history, they must relate as to their originary foundation to proto-idealizations on the substrate of a real, effectively perceived world.
units.quote: they must relate, as to their originary foundation, to *proto-idealizations on the substrate of a real, effectively perceived world* (*sur le substrat d'un monde réal effectivement perçu*).

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § II
units.term: reference back to a real founding act
units.claim: What distinguishes a tradition of truth from an arbitrary phantasm is the reference back to a real founding act, not a present percept.
units.quote: only the reference back to a real founding act distinguishes a tradition of truth from an arbitrary phantasm

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § II
units.term: worldly history presupposes the having-currency it cannot found
units.claim: As the history of its transmission does not found the value of gold, no worldly history can deliver the sense of ideal having-currency, which that history on the contrary presupposes.
units.quote: no more than the history of its transmission founds the value of gold" can any *worldly* history deliver the sense of this having-currency, since worldly history on the contrary *presupposes* it.

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § II
units.claim: Taken as singular historical origin, the founding fact would be irreplaceable and hence invariable.
units.quote: as singular historical origin, the founding fact would be irreplaceable, hence invariable*

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § II
units.term: Founding history as indissociability of fact and right
units.claim: Founding history would be the deep place of the indissociability of sense and being, of fact and right.
units.quote: Founding history would be the deep place of the *indissociability of sense and being, of fact and right*;

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § VII
units.claim: The speaking subject taken by itself is incapable of absolutely founding the ideal objectivity of sense.
units.quote: the *speaking* subject, in the narrow sense of the term, is *incapable of absolutely founding the ideal objectivity of sense*

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § VII
units.term: irreal as founded in a real yet identical across realities
units.claim: The irreal is defined as what is founded in a specific real by its spatio-temporal apparition yet can appear in different realities as identical and not merely similar.
units.quote: and *irreal* "every determination that is doubtless *founded* in a specific real by virtue of its spatio-temporal apparition, but can appear in *different* realities *as identical* — and not merely as similar"

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § VII
units.term: ideality of the signifier's form as an unthematized stratum
units.claim: The note discovers a stratum Husserl never thematized, the ideality of the signifier's form.
units.quote: it discovers a stratum Husserl never thematized (the ideality of the signifier's form — in later terms, the iterability of the mark)

units.primary_locator: Introduction à L'Origine de la géométrie, § VII
units.term: writing as condition of tradition and of forgetting
units.claim: Writing is at once the condition of the infinite tradition of truth and the condition of its forgetting, the remedy and the source of crisis being one possibility.
units.quote: Writing is at once the condition of the infinite tradition of truth *and* the condition of its forgetting; the pharmakon-structure that Derrida will analyze a decade later in Plato is here read off from Husserl's own text, where the remedy for finitude and the source of crisis are demonstrably one and the same possibility.
